title: Swan Lake
synopsis:
Act I: Prince Siegfried celebrates his 21st birthday in the palace gardens. His mother reminds him that he must choose a bride at the royal ball the following night, leaving him melancholy and yearning for freedom.

Act II: Wandering into a misty forest by a lake at night, Siegfried encounters Odette, the Swan Queen, who reveals she was cursed by the sorcerer Rothbart to live as a swan by day and human by night. Only a vow of pure, unrequited love can break the spell.

Act III: At the royal ball, Rothbart arrives in disguise with his daughter Odile, the Black Swan, who is glamorized to resemble Odette. Tricked by the illusion, Siegfried swears his love to Odile, inadvertently dooming Odette.

Act IV: Returning in despair to the lake, Siegfried begs Odette for forgiveness. When Rothbart summons a fierce storm to destroy them, their ultimate sacrifice and steadfast love shatter Rothbart's powers, vanquishing him forever.
history_and_evolution: Swan Lake premiered in 1877 with choreography by Julius Reisinger, but was considered a failure due to uninspired choreography and poor staging. Following Tchaikovsky's passing, Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov staged a monumental revival in 1895 for the Mariinsky Theatre. Ivanov choreographed the poetic, lyrical 'white acts' (Acts II and IV), while Petipa choreographed the court scenes, establishing it as the ultimate foundational pillar of classical ballet.

title: The Nutcracker
synopsis:
Act I: On Christmas Eve during a festive family gathering, young Clara Stahlbaum receives a wooden nutcracker toy from her mysterious godfather, Drosselmeyer. At midnight, the parlor undergoes a magical transformation as the Christmas tree grows to monumental proportions. An army of aggressive mice attacks, led by the Mouse King. The Nutcracker leads toy soldiers into battle, and Clara helps defeat the Mouse King by throwing her slipper, causing the Nutcracker to transform into a handsome Prince.

Act II: The Prince guides Clara through the shimmering Snow Forest into the enchanted Land of Sweets. They are greeted by the Sugar Plum Fairy, who hosts a grand celebration of international dances from around the world (Spanish, Arabian, Chinese, Russian, and French). The ballet concludes with the majestic Waltz of the Flowers and the grand pas de deux.
history_and_evolution: Based on E.T.A. Hoffmann's dark tale adapted by Alexandre Dumas père. While Tchaikovsky's score was celebrated for its innovative orchestration (including the introduction of the newly invented celesta), the original 1892 staging received mixed reviews. George Balanchine's 1954 choreography for the New York City Ballet transformed the work into a beloved American holiday tradition, setting a global standard for festive family ballet.
key_variations: Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy

historical_performances.theater: New York City Center, New York
historical_performances.relevance: Popularized the work globally, establishing the modern North American holiday performance tradition.

title: The Sleeping Beauty
synopsis:
Prologue: At Princess Aurora's christening, the evil fairy Carabosse, furious at being omitted from the guest list, curses Aurora to prick her finger on a spindle and die. The Lilac Fairy commutes the sentence to a century-long sleep.

Act I: On her 16th birthday, Aurora dances with four royal suitors (The Rose Adagio). Carabosse disguises herself, hands Aurora a spindle, and the curse takes effect, sending the kingdom into a deep slumber.

Act II: One hundred years later, Prince Florimund is guided by the Lilac Fairy through a mystical vision of Aurora. He reaches the hidden castle and awakens Aurora with love's kiss.

Act III: A lavish royal wedding takes place, attended by fairytale figures including Puss in Boots, Red Riding Hood, and the Bluebird, culminating in Aurora and Florimund's Grand Pas de Deux.
history_and_evolution: Considered the crowning achievement of 19th-century Imperial Russian ballet. Petipa provided Tchaikovsky with exhaustive rhythmic and structural instructions for every bar of music. The work demands flawless academic line, endurance, and noble carriage, serving as the benchmark for classical technique.

historical_performances.choreographer: Marius Petipa (staged by Ninette de Valois)
historical_performances.relevance: Reopened the Royal Opera House after WWII, starring Margot Fonteyn.

title: Giselle
synopsis:
Act I: Giselle, a fragile peasant girl with a weak heart, falls in love with Loys, unaware he is Duke Albrecht in disguise. When the jealous gamekeeper Hilarion exposes Albrecht's noble identity and betrothal to Princess Bathilde, Giselle suffers a tragic breakdown and dies of a broken heart.

Act II: At midnight by Giselle's grave, Myrtha, Queen of the Wilis (vengeful spirits of brides betrayed before their wedding day), summons Giselle into their order. The Wilis force Hilarion to dance to his death. However, Giselle's enduring love protects Albrecht, enabling him to survive their death-dance until dawn breaks, dispersing the spirits.
history_and_evolution: The quintessential Romantic ballet, inspired by Heinrich Heine's legends of the Wilis and Victor Hugo's poetry. Carlotta Grisi created the title role, showcasing the revolutionary use of pointe work to embody ethereal spirituality. Marius Petipa later revised the staging for St. Petersburg, providing the definitive choreographic score preserved today.

title: Don Quixote
synopsis:

Act II: Kitri and Basilio escape to a gypsy camp. Don Quixote hallucinates, attacks a windmill, and falls into a dream vision of an enchanted garden filled with Dryads.

Act III: In a tavern, Basilio fakes suicide to trick Lorenzo into granting his blessing before 'dying'. Once blessed, Basilio miraculously recovers, leading to a glorious wedding feast featuring their famous Grand Pas de Deux.
history_and_evolution: Based on episodes from Miguel de Cervantes' masterpiece. Petipa created the initial Moscow staging, but Alexander Gorsky's 1900 revival for the Bolshoi introduced dynamic naturalism, crowd acting, and theatrical realism. Minkus's vibrant score is celebrated for its rhythmic Spanish color and virtuosic display.

historical_performances.relevance: Revolutionized classical mime with organic ensemble movement and dramatic realism.

title: La Sylphide
synopsis:

Act II: In the enchanted forest, Madge gives James a magical scarf, claiming it will bind the Sylphide's wings to him. When James wraps the scarf around her, her wings fall off and she dies in his arms. As her spirit ascends, James looks back to see Effie marrying his rival Gurn.
